description: A dual-voice bytebeat synthesiser running the Keeos Ogham hardware module's own firmware: each voice plays one of a hundred short integer formulas on a shared time base

params.text: Sets Parameter A, a number from 0 to 255 that both voices read; what it changes depends on the formula each voice is running
Sets Parameter B, a number from 0 to 255 that both voices read; what it changes depends on the formula each voice is running
Sets the playback rate: free running it goes from a sixty-fourth of speed at fully counter-clockwise through unity at noon to sixty-four times at fully clockwise
A lo-fi macro that is clean at the centre: turned down it filters and folds, turned up it crushes and adds resonance
Says what the Clk/VOct jack carries: at Clk it is a clock that drives the time base, and at VOct it is a pitch at a volt per octave

inputs.text: Added to the A knob, a fifth of the knob's travel per volt, with the total held between the ends; the CV to Tone field can take it away from A and point it at the Tone macro
Added to the B knob, a fifth of the knob's travel per volt, with the total held between the ends; the CV to Tone field can take it away from B and point it at the Tone macro
A rising edge above 1V puts the time base back to zero and plucks the low-pass gate, which is silent unless the LPG decay field is above zero
A clock the time base follows, or a pitch at a volt per octave, according to the Clk/VOct switch; in VOct mode no edges are taken from it at all

outputs.text: Voice 1 after the tone macro, the effects chain and the low-pass gate, 5V at full scale and a little over on peaks
Voice 2 after the tone macro, the effects chain and the low-pass gate, 5V at full scale and a little over on peaks
An envelope follower on one of the two voices, or that voice's bytebeat straight out as a voltage, 0-10V; the CV Out mode field picks which of the four
A 10V gate following the tempo the module works out for itself from voice 1's rhythm

notes: turning the Func encoder changes the function of the selected voice, a click swaps which voice is selected, and holding it about 0.6 seconds opens the Menu and leaves it
the Func encoder is not a Rack parameter, so clicking it cannot reach this help and Rack's MIDI mapper cannot reach the two function slots; the right-click menu lists every function by name
the scroll wheel turns the Func encoder only while Rack's own Scroll wheel knob adjustment preference is on, and a drag turns it unless Drag turns the encoder is switched off
the display reads the selected voice and its function as X-NN, and in the Menu the effect, field and value as T x. NN; the dot at the far right means the Tone macro is at its clean centre
with a clock patched into Clk the Rate knob snaps to a division or multiplication of it, a thirty-second up to thirty-two times; pulling the cable holds that rate until the knob moves
with the switch at VOct the Rate knob becomes a fine tune of one octave either way, added to the pitch input, and the formula is played faster or slower rather than restarted
the last function in the bank is a 440Hz reference tone, and while a voice is on it that voice runs at unity whatever the Rate knob, the clock or the pitch input say
the module is monophonic: every jack is read and written as a single channel
menu: Voice 1 function — picks voice 1's formula from the whole bank by name, grouped as Textural, Noise, Percussive, Rhythmic and Melodic, with the 440Hz reference at the end
Voice 2 function — picks voice 2's formula from the whole bank by name, grouped as Textural, Noise, Percussive, Rhythmic and Melodic, with the 440Hz reference at the end
Drag turns the encoder — lets a mouse drag over the Func encoder turn it; the setting is kept for this computer rather than in the patch
Open the Menu — does what holding the Func encoder does, and reads Leave the Menu while the Menu is open
Settings — shows all 22 Menu fields at once with their values, instead of walking them four digits at a time
FX chain: Off, On — switches the whole three-stage effects chain in and out
Chain topology: Serial, Parallel — wires the chorus, flanger and phaser one after another, or side by side
Chorus level — sets how much chorus is mixed in, 0 to 99, and 0 skips the stage entirely
Chorus type: Clean, Ensemble — one chorus voice, or three detuned ones
Chorus rate — sets how fast the chorus sweeps, 0 to 99
Chorus depth — sets how far the chorus sweeps, 0 to 99
Flanger level — sets how much flanger is mixed in, 0 to 99, and 0 skips the stage entirely
Flanger type: Clean, Barber-pole — a sweep that turns round at each end, or one that only ever climbs
Flanger rate — sets how fast the flanger sweeps, 0 to 99; 50 stops a barber-pole sweep
Flanger feedback — sets how much of the flanger's output goes back into it, 0 to 99
Phaser level — sets how much phaser is mixed in, 0 to 99, and 0 skips the stage entirely
Phaser type: Clean, Bi-phase — four poles, or eight poles with a second sweep
Phaser rate — sets how fast the phaser sweeps, 0 to 99
Phaser 2nd LFO — sets the second sweep's ratio to the first in Bi-phase, 0 to 99
CV Out mode: Envelope of Out 1, Envelope of Out 2, Out 1 as DC, Out 2 as DC — chooses what the CV Out jack carries
CV slew rise — slows how fast the CV Out can rise, from off up to about 5 seconds
CV slew fall — slows how fast the CV Out can fall, set apart from the rise
CV hold: Off, 2 ticks, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 — samples the CV Out and holds it for that many ticks, in the two DC modes only
LPG decay — sets how long the low-pass gate takes to close after a Sync pluck, 0 switching it off and 1 to 99 running 2ms to 20 seconds
CV to Tone: Off, CV A, CV B — takes one of the two CV inputs off its parameter and uses it to modulate the Tone macro
Parameter smoothing: Off, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 — crossfades A and B across a grid of that many steps rather than changing them at once
Out 2 drone: Coupled, Frozen — freezes voice 2 at its current rate and parameters so it runs on independently of the knobs

inputs.0:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.1:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.2:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.3:
1V per octave · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
